info.name: Ignition Dashboard — Backend QA
info.description:
Every request in docs/manual-qa.md, pre-built. Folder numbers match the manual-qa
section numbers, so you can run the two side by side.

Tokens and ids are captured automatically into collection variables - you never paste a
token by hand. Before you start, the server must be running (`npm run dev` in backend/).

--- THE ENVELOPE (§5) ---
Every /api response is { success, data } or { success, error: { code, message } }. A
collection-level post-response script asserts that on EVERY request, so an envelope
regression fails everywhere at once. GET /health is the one documented exception.

--- WHICH FOLDERS ARE RE-RUNNABLE ---
Folders 9-14, 16 and 17 are self-contained and safe to re-run: they log in (or
register-or-reuse) their own accounts and create their own data.

Folders 1-8 are the older schedule/auth QA and are NOT re-runnable: 2.1, 4a and 4b assert
201 on registration, so they come back 409 once those accounts exist.

--- FOLDER 16 NEEDS ONE COMMAND-LINE STEP ---
Teams have no HTTP routes at all (§5 lists no teamRouter), so the QA teams are made with
a script. Run 16.0.1-16.0.4 to create the accounts, then, from the repo:

  cd backend
  node src/scripts/manageTeams.js create "QA Team Alpha"
  node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Alpha" qa-alpha-1@example.com
  node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Alpha" qa-alpha-2@example.com
  node src/scripts/manageTeams.js create "QA Team Beta"
  node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Beta"  qa-beta-1@example.com

Then run the rest of folder 16. There is no folder 15 - manual-qa §15 is Teams, which is
command line only and always will be.

--- SHARED DATABASE ---
ignition-dashboard-dev belongs to the whole team. Folders 8, 11 and 17 put it back the
way they found it. Folder 14 rewrites the single hackathon config document and restores
it in 14.16 - if you stop that folder half way, set the dates again by hand.

item.name: 16 — Project submissions (manual-qa §16)
item.description:
Project Submission (§1.2.4).

/!\ ONE COMMAND-LINE STEP FIRST. A submission belongs to a TEAM, and teams have no HTTP routes at all (§5 lists no teamRouter, so they are provisioned by a script the way §7 provisions elevated roles).

Run 16.0.1-16.0.4 FIRST so the four QA accounts exist, then run these from the repo:

cd backend
node src/scripts/manageTeams.js create "QA Team Alpha"
node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Alpha" qa-alpha-1@example.com
node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Alpha" qa-alpha-2@example.com
node src/scripts/manageTeams.js create "QA Team Beta"
node src/scripts/manageTeams.js add    "QA Team Beta"  qa-beta-1@example.com

...then run the rest of the folder. If you skip this, 16.0.11 fails with a message saying so, and everything after it is meaningless.

WHY ITS OWN TEAMS. manual-qa §16 is written around "QA Team" / "QA Team Two" and the accounts you already have. This folder uses four accounts of its own instead, so it stays re-runnable and cannot collide with a hand-run section 15: a submission is per TEAM, so sharing "QA Team" would mean sharing its one submission slot. The mapping to the manual-qa rows:
  hacker1           = qa-alpha-1@example.com  (QA Team Alpha)
  hacker2           = qa-alpha-2@example.com  (QA Team Alpha)
  hacker3, no team  = qa-noteam@example.com   (16.2, 16.6, 16.17)
  other-team hacker = qa-beta-1@example.com   (QA Team Beta - 16.18, 16.24)

There is no folder 15: manual-qa §15 is Teams, which is command line only.
